title: From Words to Sentences
exits: Child produces three pattern families independently across two different sessions.
Child reads ten CVC words aloud that the child already uses in speech.

activities.title: Color hunt
activities.how: Ask the child to find something of a named color nearby and answer with the pattern This is a ___.

activities.title: Counting game
activities.how: Count familiar objects one by one together up to ten, letting the child say the numbers, then ask how many there are.

activities.title: Animal sounds
activities.how: Say an animal and its sound, have the child answer with the animal, then swap roles so the child leads.

assessment.ask: Ask what the child can do, and have them answer with I can ___ in a full sentence.
Point out a nearby object and have the child say This is a ___ about it.
Ask what the child likes and have them answer with I like ___.
Ask how the child feels and have them answer with I am ___.
Describe a picture and have the child say what they see with I see ___.
Name three things in the room and have the child add a color word before each one.
Have the child count five objects aloud without help.
Have the child name the animals they know from a described picture.
Mime one action and have the child say the action word in a short sentence.
Show or spell three short a words and have the child read them aloud: cat, hat, map.

goals: Name one feeling word when asked.
Notice that mistakes are part of learning.
Show curiosity by asking what a word means.
checkin: Ask how the child feels today and have them answer with one feeling word: happy, sad, tired, or excited.
Name two feeling words and let the child pick which one fits them today.
praise: You listened carefully before you answered.
You tried again after a tricky word.
You found the right word for your idea.
You said it clearly enough for me to understand.
You joined in without being asked.
You remembered that word from before.
encourage: It is fine to think before you answer.
Every mistake teaches us the next step.

calm.title: Balloon breathing
calm.how: Guide one slow breath: breathe in while lifting the arms, breathe out slowly. Then return to one very easy word.

calm.title: Quiet animal
calm.how: Ask the child to pick a calm animal and make its slow sound together, then say one easy word in that animal voice.
